---
title: "Current implementation"
---

## Package boundary

Cellerator is an early PyTorch extension for cellular dynamical model building. It adds reusable numerical operations and execution semantics where cellular identity, relations, repeated structure, conditional activity, or layout change the useful computation. PyTorch remains the foundation for ordinary tensor operations, standard modules, autograd, optimizers, and composition.

Implemented facilities have different backend and maturity boundaries. A source file or namespace does not by itself establish a supported package capability. Sparse indexing, support, routing, and gating are promising early work; they do not establish a complete adaptive runtime or a general speedup.

## Available package surfaces

- The host Python package provides native CPU Product2 and a `torch.nn.Module` adapter for CPU FP32 vectors with first-order input and coefficient gradients.
- Optional CUDA indexed-mechanism and sparse-support components have their own builds, contracts, and evidence.
- Prepared entity-to-mechanism routing is opt-in. The established Python route remains the default.
- ATen tokenization is optional and caller-directed; it does not assign biological interpretation to tokens or events.
- `ExecutionField` is an experimental CPU composition of prepared Product2 operations. It has explicit structure rebinding, but no JIT, live recompilation, or general compiler contract.
- AnnData is a required Python dependency, but no direct AnnData preparation adapter is implemented. Classical single-cell analysis remains upstream in Scanpy and RAPIDS-singlecell.

See the [Python binding guide](development/python-bindings.md), [sparse-support reference](sparse_support_foundation.qmd), [tokenization reference](tokenization.qmd), and [experimental fields note](development/experimental-fields.md) for contracts. The [source routing guide](development/routing.md) identifies current owners; the [developer reference](developer_reference.qmd) describes build and validation routes.

## Prepared routing evidence boundary

The frozen prepared-routing binary passed its 16-test correctness suite, exact CUDA correctness checks, and Compute Sanitizer memcheck, racecheck, and synccheck. The source-bound report measured a bounded lifecycle improvement for synthetic ranked `[32,8]` inputs at reuse horizon 64; the event result was inconclusive, and dense Torch was faster at larger stress shapes. Prepared routing remains opt-in, has a substantial cold-first cost, and is not evidence of a full-model or biological speedup. See the [qualification report](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/94c534fc794fe8cc3e0434e4a50f379401ddbb3c/bench/sparse_support/experiments/prepared_routing/REPORT.md) and [frozen correctness receipt](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/main/planning/coherence/qualification/cuda/complete-correctness-fixed-state.json).

Other source-bound sparse, tokenization, layout, and performance records retain their own workload and validation limits. The [reference and history index](experiments_and_history.qmd) routes those pages. The prior dated implementation record is preserved in [historical snapshot](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/main/docs/history/current_implementation_2026-10-28.qmd).

## Gaps

Cellerator is not near complete. The implemented `nn` set is small; the package has no direct AnnData preparation adapter; execution fields, compiler/IR integration, and broader adaptive execution remain experimental; and no package-wide training, biological-validity, or GPU speedup claim is established. Add model operations when a reusable contract and consumer exist, and add a `torch.nn.Module` when parameter ownership or model composition needs it. Keep correctness, scientific validity, usability, and performance claims separate and bounded by their evidence.
